To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the genetic diagnosis of FH in Czech patients has improved in recent years, and the use of international databases has contributed to this.

1) FH is one of the common monogenic diseases; 2) FH is associated with an increased risk of atherosclerosis and cardiovascular disease; 3) the FH phenotype can be caused by variants in three genes (LDLR, APOB, PCSK9) and other genes, or by a combination of common cholesterol-increase alleles (polygenic hypercholesterolaemia); 4) the prevalence of FH is high (0.2%); 5)
the genetic background of FH is complex, and that FH patients should be identified and treated as early as possible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of FH and the identification of the genetic causes of the disease in the Czech population.
the detection of FH and other lipid disorders, and the development of genetic testing for FH and other lipid abnormalities.
the genetic causes of hypercholesterolemic states, the detection of FH, and the development of novel therapeutic approaches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FH is a complex disease with many genetic and non-genetic factors that affect its clinical presentation and the risk of its complications.
FH is a complex disease with a multifactorial etiology, but the genetic basis of FH can be identified in 90% of patients.
the genetic diagnosis of FH is a key factor for the prevention of cardiovascular diseases and should be performed as early as possible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FH is a heterogeneous disease, and its genetic diagnosis is still challenging.
FH is a common monogenic disease, and its detection is crucial for the prevention of premature cardiovascular events in patients and their families.
the Czech Republic is a successful country in the field of FH diagnostics and treatment, but the number of FH patients remains unknown.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the detection of FH is a complex task, and it requires a comprehensive approach.
the use of next-generation sequencing (NGS) is a powerful tool for FH diagnostics, especially in cases of atypical FH phenotypes.

genetic testing is a valuable tool for the diagnosis and management of FH patients and that genetic testing is not a one-time event but rather an ongoing process that should be performed regularly to monitor the effectiveness of treatment and to prevent the emergence of new variants.
